title: Data Table with Sort and Filter
description: Build a data table that displays rows and columns, supports sorting by column, filtering by value, and pagination.

steps.title: Define the table data structure
steps.description: Create a `columns` array of column names and a `rows` array of data objects. Populate with at least 6 sample rows. Log the column names and row count.

codeTemplate.python:
columns = ["Name", "Age", "City", "Salary"]

rows = [
  {"Name": "Alice", "Age": 30, "City": "New York", "Salary": 75000},
  {"Name": "Bob", "Age": 25, "City": "San Francisco", "Salary": 82000},
  {"Name": "Charlie", "Age": 35, "City": "Chicago", "Salary": 68000},
  {"Name": "Diana", "Age": 28, "City": "New York", "Salary": 72000},
  {"Name": "Eve", "Age": 32, "City": "Seattle", "Salary": 90000},
  {"Name": "Frank", "Age": 40, "City": "Chicago", "Salary": 95000}
]

print("Columns:", ", ".join(columns))
print("Rows:", len(rows))

verification.successMessage: Table data structure set up with columns and 6 data rows!
verification.failureMessage: Create columns array and rows array with at least 6 sample data objects.

steps.title: Render the table as a formatted grid
steps.description: Write a `renderTable` function that returns a formatted string: each column value padded with spaces, columns separated by `|`, and a separator line after the header. Log the result.
hints: Calculate max width for each column: Math.max(header.length, ...row values)

verification.successMessage: Table renders with header, rows, and separators!
verification.failureMessage: renderTable should format the table with '|' column separators, padding, and a header separator line.

steps.title: Sort the table by a column
steps.description: Write a `sortByColumn` function that takes a `column` name and an `ascending` boolean (default true), and returns a new sorted copy of the rows. Log the sorted results.
hints: Sort with comparator: if ascending, a[col] > b[col] ? 1 : -1
For strings, use .localeCompare() or string comparison

codeTemplate.python:
columns = ["Name", "Age", "Salary"]
rows = [
  {"Name": "Charlie", "Age": 35, "Salary": 68000},
  {"Name": "Alice", "Age": 30, "Salary": 75000},
  {"Name": "Bob", "Age": 25, "Salary": 82000}
]

def sortByColumn(rows, column, ascending=True):
  

sorted = sortByColumn(rows, "Name", True)
print("Sorted by Name:", ", ".join([r["Name"] for r in sorted]))
sorted2 = sortByColumn(rows, "Salary", False)
print("Sorted by Salary desc:", ", ".join([r["Name"] + " ($" + str(r["Salary"]) + ")" for r in sorted2]))

steps.title: Filter the table by a value
steps.description: Write a `filterByValue` function that takes a `column` and a search `value`, and returns rows where the column's value contains the search string (case-insensitive). Log the filtered results.
hints: Convert both the cell value and search string to lowercase

verification.successMessage: Case-insensitive filtering by column value works!
verification.failureMessage: filterByValue(rows, 'City', 'new') should return Alice (New York) and Diana (New York).

steps.title: Paginate the results
steps.description: Write a `paginate` function that takes `page` (1-indexed) and `pageSize` (default 5), and returns the subset of rows for that page along with total page count. Log the page data and total pages.
hints: Return: { data: rows.slice(start, end), page, pageSize, totalPages: Math.ceil(rows.length / pageSize) }
If page is out of range, return empty data

codeTemplate.python:
import json

columns = ["Name", "Age"]
rows = [
  {"Name": "Row 1", "Age": 1},
  {"Name": "Row 2", "Age": 2},
  {"Name": "Row 3", "Age": 3},
  {"Name": "Row 4", "Age": 4},
  {"Name": "Row 5", "Age": 5},
  {"Name": "Row 6", "Age": 6},
  {"Name": "Row 7", "Age": 7}
]

def paginate(rows, page, pageSize=5):
  

page1 = paginate(rows, 1, 3)
print("Page 1:", json.dumps([r["Name"] for r in page1["data"]]))
print("Total pages:", page1["totalPages"])
page3 = paginate(rows, 3, 3)
print("Page 3:", json.dumps([r["Name"] for r in page3["data"]]))

verification.successMessage: Pagination returns correct data for each page with total page count!
verification.failureMessage: paginate(rows, 1, 3) should return first 3 rows. Total pages should be 3 (7 rows / 3 = 2.33, rounded up to 3).
